rows.en:
And she got even more absorbed in fortune-telling.
What was she telling fortunes about?
Suzuki.
You can't forget someone that easily, right?
What he was doing right now, what his luck would be tomorrow... she did all kinds of readings about him.{p}

Then one day, one of those readings came true.
It said Suzuki would get hurt, and that very day he fell on the stairs and sprained his ankle.
Hirai made a huge fuss, but nobody took her seriously.
"Well, I guess they do come true once in a while."
That's how it got brushed off.
After that, Hirai kept on reading Suzuki's fortune.
And some of the readings started coming true.
Only the ominous ones, too.
Losing a match, getting hurt... only the bad results came true.{p}

Naturally, everyone got creeped out, and there was even a rumor going around that Hirai was putting a curse on him.
Even though Hirai was only doing her readings like always.
Come on, a big baby like her couldn't curse anybody.
Her readings started coming true...
That's what I said just now, but strictly speaking, there was someone who made reality play out the way her readings said.
Someone who loved Hirai and hated Suzuki for making her sad.
That's right! It was her big brother.
His precious little sister had come home crying, so as her big brother, he couldn't forgive Suzuki for causing it.
So he took revenge on Suzuki, exactly the way Hirai's readings said.
Pushing him down the stairs, making prank calls the night before a match... I bet he did some pretty dangerous stuff.
In the end, Suzuki transferred to another school, even though graduation was right around the corner.
He figured his life would be in danger if he stayed at this school.
Because nobody ever suspected that Hirai's brother was the culprit.
I bet even Suzuki himself didn't know, right?{p}

Hee hee hee, you've got a 'how come?' look on your face.
You think it's weird that I know who did it?
My big sister had a crush on Hirai's brother, you see.
And while she was always watching him, she happened to see him push Suzuki down.
He was the guy she admired, so she didn't tell anyone and kept it a secret.
That's why nobody noticed what he was doing, not Suzuki, and not even his own sister, Hirai.{p}

But not knowing things is scary, isn't it?
As Suzuki was leaving for his new school, Hirai went and told him,
"All the bad luck you've had, Suzuki, it was all punishment for going against fate.
I was your goddess of good luck, but you called me weird, so you had to be punished."
That's what she said, apparently.
I don't know what happened to Suzuki after that, but it seems the Hirai siblings are still living happily together.
What is fortune-telling, anyway?
You might think it's advice for living a better life, but more people end up getting jerked around by it, don't they?
Suzuki got dragged right into it...
That's why it's scary.{p}

You'd better be careful too, {a}.
Most girls love fortune-telling, after all.
Hee hee hee.
I guess I'll end my story about here...
So what will you do? The seventh one still isn't here.
Right, {a}?{p}

Suzuki told her he wanted to break up.
He felt he just couldn't put up with a girl like her.
Hirai didn't want that.
She said she'd fix anything that was wrong with her.
But when Suzuki told her to quit fortune-telling, she said she couldn't do that.
They just went around in circles.{p}

So in the end, the two of them broke up.
Hirai was heartbroken.
It had ended with Suzuki way too soon.
And she went right back to being her big brother's little girl.
From the very next day, she started talking about nothing but her brother.{p}

Ugh, I don't like that kind of thing.
Cooking, cleaning, laundry...
Tying a woman down with that stuff, I don't know about that.
So, {a}.{p}What's your second priority, then?
Looks
Personality

Hmm.
Looks, huh.
So personality comes third.
If I'd asked about a girlfriend instead, I bet you'd put them in a different order.
Like, looks might end up coming first.
Oh, right, about Hirai's story...{p}

...Just kidding.
You can say that, but faces matter too, right?
That's what you think, isn't it?
...Oh, whatever.{p}

Everyone has all kinds of different tastes, right?
But Hirai's ideal was really unusual.
Want me to tell you?
Hirai's ideal was...{p}

Bzzzt, wrong!
It was a teacher who'd just come to our school.{p}

"Mr. Kondo, Hirai was watching just now."
"N-no, you've got it wrong.
There's really nothing between Hirai and me."
Mr. Kondo was in a total panic.
But he properly explained it to the other teachers.
How the whole thing had come about.
Every teacher in the faculty room was shocked to hear it.
Could something like that really happen? they wondered.
But the principal listened to Mr. Kondo's story seriously and said this:
"In that case, you can't leave things as they are.
You mustn't make a promise like that when you have no intention of marrying her.
Now, hurry after Hirai and talk it over with her properly."
That's what the principal said.{p}

So Mr. Kondo went looking for Hirai, who'd run off.
He raced all over the school.
But she was hard to find.
She wasn't in the classrooms or out on the school grounds.{p}

Mr. Kondo went back to the faculty room.
"H-Hirai isn't anywhere..."
he said.
"Maybe Hirai has already gone home.
We can talk again tomorrow..."
Then the principal glared at Mr. Kondo.
"Have you looked in the old school building?"
the principal asked.{p}

Mr. Kondo headed for the old school building.
Because the principal had urged him to.
The inside of the old building was falling apart, thick with the smell of mold and wood.
The wooden floors and walls were pretty rotten.
Jagged splinters poked out of holes here and there.
And the hallway creaked and groaned.
Mr. Kondo moved forward one step at a time.
Was Hirai really in here?
Hadn't she gone home after all?
That's what he was thinking.
And then...{p}

Someone slid their arms around him from behind.
Around Mr. Kondo's neck.
"H-Hirai...?"
Mr. Kondo blurted out.
Those hands were rough and hard.
They didn't seem like a schoolgirl's hands at all...{p}

"Mr. Kondo...?"
A voice came from inside a nearby classroom.
It was Hirai's voice.
She was crying.
He could hear her sniffling through the door.
But...
Mr. Kondo couldn't move from where he stood in the hallway.
Because someone was holding his neck from behind...
"That won't do, Mr. Kondo, making a schoolgirl cry.
Honestly, you are a hopeless man..."{p}

Mr. Kondo's neck was squeezed tighter and tighter.
"Honestly.
You really are hopeless.
A lovely student like Hirai..."
"P-please st... urk!"
"Why on earth would a dreary man like you be Hirai's destined partner, I wonder..."{p}

"P-Principal..."
...{p}

Mr. Kondo was found lying in the old school building the next day.
He'd been strangled to death.
And Hirai was dead too.
She was found dead, slumped over on top of Mr. Kondo.
The school apparently stuck to the story that Hirai and the teacher had an accident in the old school building.
What do you think it means?
...{a}.
Did you know the principal at our school changes a lot?
Like, our school has crazy paranormal stuff going on, right?
So I hear our principals and board chairmen are always having accidents or going out of their minds.
The principal from when Hirai was here is gone now too.
That principal really liked Hirai and used to dote on her...
But apparently, ever since the Hirai incident, the principal has vanished without a trace.
What do you think that means?{p}

Hey, {a}.
Mr. Kondo really was Hirai's destined partner, wasn't he?
The two of them were together until death, after all.
But maybe she'd have been better off never knowing about that fortune.
Then...
she wouldn't have gone chasing after Mr. Kondo and ended up like that...
...
That's the end of my story.
What should we do?
The seventh one still isn't here.
Hey, {a}...?{p}

Mr. Kondo tried to act as if nothing had happened.
So he just made excuses to the teachers around him and slipped out of the faculty room in a hurry.{p}

And then...
someone suddenly tapped him on the shoulder from behind.{p}

When he turned around, there was Hirai.
She had only pretended to run off, and was waiting for Mr. Kondo in the hallway.{p}

"H-Hirai.
Didn't you go home?"
Hirai tugged at the flustered teacher's arm.
"Mr. Kondo, I need to talk to you..."
Hirai started walking, her head hanging.
"H-Hirai.
Where are we going?"
"Somewhere we can talk, just the two of us..."
Who knows what she was thinking, but Hirai took him to the gym.
Then she turned her back to him and fell silent.{p}

"A-aaaaagh☆"
Mr. Kondo grabbed the knife Hirai had dropped and stabbed her again and again in a frenzy.{p}

"Aaaaaaaaah☆"
She shrieked in agony.
"Aaagh, aaaagh☆"
Even so, Mr. Kondo kept driving the knife into her, violently.
Over and over and over.
She desperately tried to stop Mr. Kondo's hand, but...
Mr. Kondo brought the knife down on her in a frenzy.
"Uaaaaaagh☆"
Even after she stopped moving, Mr. Kondo kept swinging the knife.
And all she could do was bathe in a shower of her own blood.
"What's going on★"
A teacher outside heard Hirai's scream and came running.
And then...{p}

What was there was Mr. Kondo holding a bloody knife, and a schoolgirl lying on the floor, stabbed all over her body.
"M-Mr. Kondo...☆"
"Ah, n-no, this is..."
"Mu-murdeeerer☆"
"N-no, it's not what you think!
This is...☆"
An ambulance was called right away, but Hirai couldn't be saved.
Mr. Kondo was taken away by the police.
Apparently he confessed to all kinds of things...{p}

What he told them was a story about a beauty named Hirai falling in love with the short, dumpy Mr. Kondo.
A story about her calling him her destined partner and pressuring him to marry her.
And a story about her luring him to the gym and threatening him by pulling a nerve out of her pinky...
The case was ruled the result of Mr. Kondo's delusions.
That he'd let his fantasies about a beautiful schoolgirl swell until he finally even committed murder...{p}

Hey, {a}.
Mr. Kondo wasn't lying at all.
Hirai's behavior really had him terrified.
My big sister said so too.
She said back then, Mr. Kondo always seemed jittery and scared around Hirai.{p}

But you know...
Whatever the reason, Mr. Kondo had to pay for the crime of killing her.
So they say he quietly went along with whatever the police said.
...
Huh, {a}.
Why are you making that face?
Don't tell me you have doubts?
Do you think this whole story was just Mr. Kondo's delusion...?
Anyway, that's the end of my story.
No matter what you think.
...But they're late, aren't they?
The seventh one.
What should we do?
Hey, {a}...?{p}

Without thinking, Mr. Kondo hugged Hirai tight.
"Hirai! I'm sorry☆
It's my fault things came to this..."
Then Hirai said something like this:
"It's all right, Mr. Kondo.
We're bound together by the red thread, aren't we?
Instead of apologizing, show me your love.
Come on, show me.
Your red thread, Mr. Kondo..."
And then Hirai picked up the knife she'd dropped.{p}

"Wh... whoaaaa☆"
Startled, Mr. Kondo ran for it.{p}

Then she pounded on the door even harder.
Shouting in rage, again and again.{p}

"I'll kill you☆
I won't forgive you☆
I'll kill you☆"
she screamed.
Mr. Kondo was in a complete panic.{p}

Not understanding any of it, he just held the door shut and trembled.
After a while, her screams got even louder.
Then came the sound of voices outside, like a fierce argument.
One of the neighbors had called the police.
Amid a lot of thudding and stomping, her voice slowly faded away.
It seemed the police had restrained her and taken her off somewhere.
And the next day...{p}

Mr. Kondo was called in by the principal.
It had to be about Hirai.
Mr. Kondo swallowed hard, tense.
The principal just stared at him in silence for a while.
When Mr. Kondo couldn't stand the silence any longer and was about to speak...
the principal said only this:
"Hirai is... dead..."{p}

Hirai killed herself.
She couldn't stand the way Mr. Kondo treated her.
She did some pretty extreme things, didn't she?
Cutting her finger with a knife, chasing after Mr. Kondo...
But he treated her coldly while she was in such a fragile state.
That's why it ended up like this.{p}

And after this incident, they say the ghost of a schoolgirl holding a knife started appearing in our school gym.
They say the ghost says this:
"Shall I show you my red thread...?
Then show me yours..."
That's what she says.
It seems Hirai is still searching for her destined partner.
So she shows up not just here, but in school gyms all over the place.
Holding a glittering knife...
...{p}

That's the end of my story.
But...
They're not coming, are they, the seventh one.
What should we do?
Hey, {a}...?{p}
"G... go away!
Please! Just go away☆"{p}

Mr. Kondo screamed desperately.
And then...

The pounding on the door stopped.
And so did Hirai's voice.
Instead, he heard footsteps.
Footsteps moving away from the door.
As the footsteps faded, the terror that had reached its peak slowly began to ease.
The footsteps were gone completely.
...What should I do?
Should I open the door and check?
That's what Mr. Kondo thought.{p}So what do you think he did?
He opened the door
He didn't open the door

With trembling hands, Mr. Kondo opened the door.
And then...{p}

"Mr. Kondooo☆"
A single hand slipped in through the gap in the door.
It was Hirai's hand.
From its bloody pinky stretched a red thread of nerve.
She had been hiding behind the door.
"Waaaagh☆"
Mr. Kondo rushed to slam the door shut.
And her arm got caught in the door...{p}

"Nooooo☆"
She wailed at the top of her voice.
"Mr. Kondo, you're cruel!
Mr. Kondo, you're so cruel...☆"{p}
Over and over and over, he tried to slam the door shut...{p}

They say the bones in Mr. Kondo's arm were completely smashed.
And after the incident, he apparently quit the school like he was running away.
I wonder what Mr. Kondo's doing now.
...Right now, Hirai is living in a hospital, they say.
She seems perfectly normal.
My big sister went to visit her a few times, you see.
Hirai told her this story when she went to visit.
My sister is seven years older than me.
She's twenty-three now.
She works in an office.
But Hirai, who was her classmate, is still nineteen.
She stays nineteen forever and never gets any older, apparently.
Because once she turns twenty, she'll die.
Hirai herself believes that, so what can you do?
So her family keeps telling her she's still nineteen, forever and ever.
And apparently they're searching really hard.
For who, you ask?
Obviously.
Someone named Shinji Kondo.
Because she can't see Mr. Kondo anymore, right?{p}

He shook his head and pushed the thought away.
She might still be on the other side of the door.
So he mustn't open it.
And so he waited until night came.{p}

He held his body rigid, held his breath, strained his ears so he wouldn't miss even the tiniest sound, and waited for dawn.
It was a long night.
Every second ticked off by the clock hands crawled by, like slow motion.
And at some point, Mr. Kondo fell asleep.
As time went by, the tension wore off and he let his guard down, you know.
But in the middle of the night, a suspicious noise woke him up.
Something was rustling around in the room.{p}

He rubbed his sleepy eyes and looked closely, and there was Hirai, standing right in front of him!
Mr. Kondo was instantly wide awake, but no voice came out.
"...Mr. Kondo.
I have a spare key, so I let myself in.
Hey, Mr. Kondo.
You said you'd marry me, so why were you so cold to me?
I can't forgive you. Now you have to swallow a thousand needles..."{p}

"F-forgive me!
It was my fault!
Hirai, please forgive me☆"
Mr. Kondo apologized to Hirai over and over.
And then...{p}
